items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Mitchell Ayres was the musical director. ... I was the first black musician to be in the band on ABC ... Mitchell Ayres was the bandleader.

ctx.x: Can you give us some insights as to how he worked in the studio, was he a fast worker, did he do a lot of takes?

No, he didn’t do too many takes. He knew what he wanted to do before he got there. Evidently, he had gotten with Sy Oliver before the record date and Sy wrote the arrangements according to what Pops’ ideas were. So, we just ran through them, he didn’t take no time. It didn’t take any time at all for him to do that. I wouldn’t have cared anyway if he had taken 10 hours because I was having a ball up there, watching how he played. He used to come to hear me play when he’d come to California here, I had a little gig…

Ayres was the musical director. He used to come over and sit down and tell me a lot of jokes, ‘cause he and Basie were very good friends. He and Basie were very, very, very good friends. I didn’t know that so many of the older musicians were as tight as they were because the road was the only life that we knew. And I remember when Duke was very sick, they were making this “I Love You Madly” TV show here at Century City and I went out there and I was sitting with Basie and I found out that he and Duke had been…

items.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I went back and I got a studio job here at ABC, with Mitchell Ayres on the Hollywood Palace

ctx.x: How many years did you spend with the Basie band?

Well from ‘38 until 1950, then I went back and I got a studio job here at ABC, with Mitchell Ayres on the Hollywood Palace, and then I started playing with Frank Sinatra. I did everything with him and Nelson Riddle for about 13 years. I recorded a lot with Nat King Cole, Ella Fitzgerald. I’ve been blessed all my life. It seems like that I don’t know why I’ve been called to do records that like anybody could have done it you know.

Yeah, but like you stated, you had your sound. You must have developed a sound that people recognized and that when Frank Sinatra did a date, he knew who he wanted to hear behind him, as did Nelson Riddle.

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: I was promised a studio job at ABC with Mitchell Ayres, the Hollywood Palace show.

ctx.x: The Embers. Started going to the Embers and started going to the Roundtable and, you know, I just worked all around New York with a quartet for a while, you know, after

Joe and I, we terminated our association. And then I came back out here in California in 1960 -- well, I was promised a studio job at ABC with Mitchell Ayres, the Hollywood Palace show. It went on every week. I was promised that job by Johnny Fresco, the contractor, and I told Basie I had to go back to assume, you know, my work out here, you know, and I had gotten married and my daughter was -- my wife was pregnant at the time and I told him I couldn't stay too long because I had a job to go to, which was a…
So I ended up staying there a year. Then --
